title: Two declared issuers, one advertises everything and one advertises nothing
rationale: The aggregation rule, pinned. A resource that names two issuers has not given its clients a working mix-up defence if only one of the two provides it: the client picks an issuer, and RFC 9728 7.6 puts that choice out of scope, so a defence available at one of two is a coin toss. C13 already refuses the permissive reading in the same module -- "a resource that names five issuers of which four are dead is the thesis in miniature; scoring it PASS because one answered would discard the finding" -- and C14 was corrected to match on 29 July 2026. Without this fixture the difference between "all" and "any" is invisible: every other C16-C18 fixture declares a single issuer, and under one issuer the two rules agree. C18 is included here for a second reason: its aggregation genuinely was `any` until 30 July 2026, while the amendment log recorded it as `all`.

spec.quote: Secure determination of appropriate authorization servers to use with a protected resource for all use cases is out of scope for this specification.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org; the sentence that makes "one of the two issuers is safe" insufficient, because nothing determines which one the client uses. Lowercase, out-of-scope prose: it anchors no penalty, which is why all three checks here are descriptive.

spec.quote: authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: Boolean parameter indicating whether the authorization server provides the iss parameter in the authorization response as defined in Section 2. If omitted, the default value is false.
